summary: Added a first-class fx.global_load helper on fx.Tensor that supports scalar and vector results, mutually exclusive typed element or byte offsets, explicit alignment, and scalar or lane-wise masks with passthrough values. The base checkout reproduced the missing API through its public-export regression, which asserted that fx.global_load was absent.

tests.what_was_measured: 27 LLVM wrapper/export tests passed, including the new public fx.global_load export expectation. Raw output: /job/artifacts/j-1c455b82713d/unit.log

A real ROCm GPU kernel compared scalar element-offset loads, vector byte-offset loads, and masked scalar loads against independently indexed/generated Torch tensors. Raw output: /job/artifacts/j-1c455b82713d/gpu-rerun.log

Fresh compilation plus GPU numerical execution. LLVM IR contains load i32 align 4, load <4 x i32> align 16, and llvm.masked.load.v1i32.p1 with -77 passthrough. Final gfx ISA contains global_load_dword and global_load_dwordx4. Raw output: /job/artifacts/j-1c455b82713d/gpu-ir.log; IR/ISA: /job/artifacts/j-1c455b82713d/ir/global_load_kernel_0/

remaining_limitations: The helper intentionally accepts only global fx.Tensor values; existing fx.Pointer users continue to use fx.generic_load.
Cache-policy metadata was not added because it was optional in the proposal and the generic LLVM load path currently exposes only nontemporal metadata.
